summary: Not as a flip signal. On BTC, ETH and SOL, entries on a SuperTrend flip did the same as random entries on 1h, 4h and daily, with a multiplier of 2, 3 or 4. The result that holds up is the 4h trend state on the short side: while SuperTrend(10, 3) read a down trend, shorts beat random entries by 0.46% after 20 candles, and this holds without its strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles.

verdicts.use: Staying long in an up trend
verdicts.text: On 4h it beat random entries by 0.44%, but only because of the stretch between Dec 25, 2020 and Mar 12, 2021. Without that stretch it was the same as random.

verdicts.use: Staying short in a down trend
verdicts.text: On 4h it beat random entries by 0.46% after 20 candles. It holds without its strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles.

notes: On 1h, SuperTrend(10, 3) flipping up gave 1,860 entries in 1,797 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.12% ahead of random entries, inside the luck band. A multiplier of 2 flips about one and three quarters times as often as 3, and a multiplier of 4 about two thirds as often. Neither one beat random on 1h, 4h or daily.

Shorting while SuperTrend(10, 3) read a down trend on 4h gave 19,867 entries in 330 separate moves. They beat random entries by 0.46% after 20 candles. The result holds without its strongest stretch, between Apr 6 and Jun 15, 2022, and shows at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. By coin it is uneven: SOL beat random by 0.84% and BTC by 0.35%, both fragile, while ETH at 0.18% was the same as random.

The 4h short result comes from downtrends inside larger uptrends. While the pair closed above its 200-day SMA, the short beat random by 0.53% and held without its strongest stretch. Below the 200-day SMA it beat random by 0.25%, but that rests on the stretch between Apr 6 and Jun 15, 2022. It also showed only at 10 and 20 candles there, not at 50 or 100.

The long side of the same 4h trend state is fragile. Its 0.44% gap over random comes from 412 entries between Dec 25, 2020 and Mar 12, 2021, and without them it was the same as random. Split by the 200-day SMA, both halves rest on one stretch each: between Jul 21 and Sep 12, 2021 above it, and between Jan 2 and Jan 30, 2023 below it.

On 1h the trend state carries nothing. Long in an up trend and short in a down trend each came out 0.03% ahead of random, inside the band. On daily, the down-trend short was the same as random overall. It beat random by 5.17% after 20 days while the pair was above its 200-day SMA, over 42 moves, and held without its strongest stretch at 10 and 20 days but not at 50 or 100. Below the 200-day SMA it was 0.08%, the same as random.

For a DCA bot, a SuperTrend flip as the start condition times entries no better than a random candle. The bot's DCA orders and take profit do the work. The one shape worth testing is the 4h SuperTrend(10, 3) down-trend state as a filter that lets a short bot open only while it holds. It breaks below the 200-day SMA, where the result rests on one stretch. Leave the up-trend state out as a long filter on these pairs, because its result came from one rally.
